channel.title: Attention Optimization
channel.description: Technical notes by Jaehun Ryu, a deep learning compiler engineer, on LLM inference, KV caches, compilers, C++, AI papers, and open-source code.

item.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
item.description:
Paper

Introduction

Blackwell GPUs execute FP8 and FP4 matrix multiplies 2x and 4x faster than BF16, respectively. To bring that speed to attention, the first problem to solve is not precision loss but whether “a quantized value is reconstructed identically in the forward and backward computations.” FLAMIA designs this condition inside a low-bit attention kernel and turns it into training calls that are actually faster on Blackwell.

item.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
item.description:
Paper

SpecOPD: Training Speculative Decoding Drafters with Branch Parallelism

Introduction

Speculative decoding speeds up generation by having a small drafter propose multiple tokens that a large target verifies in a single pass. But the ceiling on that speed is set by how many tokens the drafter can get right in a row, and on-policy distillation, the approach aimed at this problem, is tied to sequential draft-verify rollouts while collecting its training signal. SpecOPD starts from the observation that this sequential dependence is not essential to on-policy learning.

item.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
item.description:
Paper

Introduction

A game world built by a video generation model alone stores off-screen state nowhere. Every time a corridor you have already passed through is redrawn, it changes, and rules such as health have to be read back from pixels. Matrix-Game 4.0 has the game engine enforce rules and state in code, while the video model is responsible only for rendering the screen.

item.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
item.description:
Training on long documents across several GPUs creates more than a compute problem. Each GPU also needs the right attention mask: the rules that determine which tokens may attend to which other tokens. If those rules leave one GPU with more work than the others, the entire training step waits for it.

FlashMask-3 starts with how masks are stored, then uses that representation to select work, distribute it, and overlap communication with computation. The paper reports a 7.3–11.0% improvement in full training throughput for a MoE model with a 128K context on 128 H100 GPUs. That result must be distinguished from the speedup of the attention kernel alone (§4.3, Table 1).

item.title: MC-Sparse: Deconstructing and Closing the Dense-Sparse Attention Gap in Diffusion Transformers
item.description:
Paper

TL;DR

By making the attention of a diffusion transformer (DiT) sparse at the token level without training, while caching and reusing accurate KV selections and dense–sparse output residuals at anchor steps, it achieves up to a $2.32\times$ denoising speedup in video and 3D generation with no quality loss (source: Fig. teaser, §Abstract).

item.title: Mechanics of Long-Context Hybrid Models Part 1.1: From Hybrid Attention to Hybrid Position
item.description:
Paper

Mechanics of Long-Context Hybrid Models: From Hybrid Attention to Hybrid Position

TL;DR — These days open-source LLMs are rapidly shifting from models that “use full attention only” to hybrid models that “mix full attention with Sliding-Window Attention (SWA) or Linear Attention (LA).” This paper mechanistically dissects “why” hybrid models work and “how” they can be designed better. The key conclusion is that the true identity of a hybrid model is in fact not hybrid attention but hybrid position (NoPE + position-biased attention). It identifies a Seesaw Effect — SWA hybrids are strong at length extrapolation but flip on context extension — and a No-Free-Lunch Effect — LA hybrids are strong within the training length but weak at extrapolation. As a solution it proposes Sliding-Window Linear Attention (SWLA), which extrapolates 4k→64k, i.e. 16× without training, while maintaining 100% accuracy on NIAH-SK1.

item.title: SlimKV: Joint Token-Feature KV Cache Compression with Reconstruction-Free Beacon Attention
item.description:
Paper

SlimKV: Compressing Tokens and Features Together, Cutting the KV Cache by up to 32× with Reconstruction-Free Latent-Space Attention

TL;DR

SlimKV is a question-agnostic framework that compresses the KV cache — the bottleneck of long-context LLM inference — simultaneously along the token axis and the feature axis. The key idea is to remove RoPE only from the Keys of beacon memory tokens, so attention is performed directly in the latent space without a reconstruction step. It achieves the best performance at 16×/32× compression on LongBench (source: §5.2), and at a 128K token length it delivers up to 7.34× attention speedup and 3.38× end-to-end decoding speedup over no compression (source: §5.4).

item.title: The KV Cache Is the New Memory Wall
item.description:
Paper

The KV Cache Is the New Memory Wall: Three Regimes and Five Domains of Long-Context LLM Inference

TL;DR — Long-context LLM decode inference is bound by memory bandwidth, not arithmetic, and once context length crosses a specific computable “crossover” point, the bottleneck shifts from model weights to the KV cache. This paper unifies the five families of techniques that aim to reduce the KV cache (quantization, token eviction, paging, prefix caching, tiering) into a single footprint model, derives exact crossover context lengths and speedup ceilings on roofline maps of the H100/B200/MI300X, and realigns results that were measured in different settings and could not be compared onto a single coordinate system.

item.title: MassAlloc Attention: Let Attention Allocate Its Own Compute
item.description:
Paper

MassAlloc Attention (MALA): Letting Attention Allocate Its Own Compute

TL;DR — Full softmax attention (FullAttn) performs all post-score computation after QK score generation for every causal tile, whereas MALA uses the normalized mass produced by attention itself to selectively perform post-score operations. As a result, it maintains FullAttn-level quality while reducing training forward/backward latency by $2.2\times$ / $3.0\times$ and decoding latency by $1.6\times$, and cuts total training FLOPs by $23.1\%$ in 32K long-context training of a 14B model (source: Abstract, §3).

item.title: WorldAttention: An Efficient Attention Architecture for Interactive Video World Models
item.description:
Paper

WorldAttention: System Co-Design of an Interactive Video World Model That Drops the Sliding Window

TL;DR — Text-controlled interactive video world models are trapped between the demand to “remember the entire history” and the reality that “the KV cache grows linearly until GPU memory blows up.” Researchers at Alibaba DAMO Academy solve this dilemma with an attention architecture called WorldAttention. A hierarchical KV cache (HKV) splits memory into pages and distributes them across a multi-tier memory hierarchy, a hybrid sparse attention (HSA) makes the computation linear and sparse, and custom kernels push actual hardware performance to the limit. The results are a VBench-Long subject consistency of 0.9472, an InterVBench score of 0.9668, and 22.0 FPS on a single H100 GPU (source: Abstract, Tab. 1).

item.title: Block Sparse Attention with Log-Linear Complexity
item.description:
Paper

PISA: Pyramid Top-$K$ Selection Lowers the Cost of Block-Sparse Attention to $O(N\log N)$

TL;DR — Block-sparse attention makes attention computation linear, but block selection still costs quadratic time. PISA solves this by layering keys into a pyramid via average pooling and narrowing candidates at each level with LogSumExp (LSE) scores. Prefill selection cost drops to $O(N\log N)$ and decode to $O(\log N)$, delivering up to $9.95\times$ speedup in selection latency over existing BSA at 256K tokens.

item.title: Fathom: Per-Query Read Depth for Sparse Decoding over Offloaded KV Caches
item.description:
Paper

Fathom: Accelerating 1M-Token Decoding by 1.67x with Query-Adaptive Depth Scanning

TL;DR

When agent sessions stretch to 1M tokens and dozens of sessions reside concurrently, the KV cache and the index used to rank it must live in host memory, making the top-k scan at every decode step bound by PCIe bytes (source: §1). Fathom stores the 4-bit K cache as channel-major bit-planes so that reading the leading $t$ planes yields an exact $t$-bit quantization, and each query partitions its bit budget across channels via reverse water-filling based on per-channel importance $g_j$ (source: §3.2, §3.3). On Qwen3-8B at 1M tokens with batch size 1, it is 1.67x faster in GPU time than a 136-bit scan, 2.50x faster than landmarks, and 3.12x faster than thumbnails, while achieving 1.1–5.3x lower attention error with 18% fewer bytes than SparQ r=16 at matched GPU time (source: Tab. 1, Tab. 2, Tab. 5). However, it provides no speedup when the index resides in HBM (source: §7).

item.title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
item.description:
Paper

SAS: A Simple Attention Sparsification That Learns Context Ranking Directly Without Distillation

TL;DR — In post-training attention sparsification, inject the continuous scores produced by the selector into the attention logits as a log gate. This bypasses the gradients blocked by discrete Top-K selection, allowing the selector to be trained end-to-end with the language modeling loss, without auxiliary distillation. As a result, at a tight budget (1024 tokens), it lifts GPQA-Diamond by up to +15.5 points over SeerAttention-R on Qwen3-4B/8B/14B, and cuts decoding latency by up to 5.6× at 512K context.

item.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
item.description:
Linear Attention Rewritten with a Kalman Filter: Kalman Delta Networks

TL;DR

The fixed-size recurrent memory update of linear attention is reinterpreted as a linear-Gaussian state-space model, and the covariance tracking of the optimal estimator, the Kalman filter, is introduced to decide “how strongly to overwrite” based on uncertainty, yielding Kalman Delta Networks (KDN). DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, and KDA reduce to fixed-gain special cases that omit the covariance, and KDN outperforms every SOTA linear recurrent mixer evaluated at 750M/1.3B pretraining in both PPL and average accuracy (source: Abstract, §1).

item.title: [Paper Review] Hardware-Efficient Attention for Fast Decoding
item.description:
Paper

GTA & GLA: Hardware-Efficient Attention That Breaks the ‘Memory-Dominated’ Decode

TL;DR

GTA (key–value tying) and GLA (latent head sharding) raise FLOPs/byte and shrink the per-GPU KV cache, achieving 1.2–2× kernel speedups, sharply lower serving latency, and up to 2× higher throughput — without quality loss (source: §Abstract, Fig.4–5, Fig.15, Tab.38–41).

item.title: [Paper Review] Llama-Nemotron: Efficient Reasoning Models
item.description:
Paper Link

Hydragen: The Secret Weapon for Decoding Large Batches with Shared Prefixes up to 32× Faster

TL;DR

By decomposing the prefix and suffix using softmax denominator rescaling, Hydragen accelerates long-context, large-batch decoding on Code-Llama-13B by up to 32x compared to vLLM, all while guaranteeing bit-for-bit identical output.
